headline: This file declares 2 spaces, 3 role declarations, 3 named types and 12 functions.

items.name: Concepts
items.signature: space Concepts = MAP[8192]
summary: A value of `Concepts` is a list of 8192 numbers, where every position holds either +1 or -1, and two of them are combined by multiplying position against position. Nothing about that list means anything on its own; its meaning is which other values it was built from.

Several values can be added together into a single one, which is what `load` counts everywhere below. That only works up to a point. Past it, asking for one of the items back returns a different item instead, and nothing fails while it happens.
For `Concepts` that point is 352 items. It was measured at 95% retrieval, not derived from a formula.
The declaration also records seed and codebook.

items.name: Phases
items.signature: space Phases = FHRR[1024]
summary: A value of `Phases` is a list of 1024 numbers, where every position holds an angle, and two of them are combined by adding their angles. Nothing about that list means anything on its own; its meaning is which other values it was built from.

Several values can be added together into a single one, which is what `load` counts everywhere below. That only works up to a point. Past it, asking for one of the items back returns a different item instead, and nothing fails while it happens.
For `Phases` that point is 31 items. It was measured at 95% retrieval, not derived from a formula.
The declaration also records seed.

items.name: Subject, Verb, Object
items.signature: role Subject, Verb, Object in Concepts
summary: Subject, Verb and Object are fixed values of `Concepts`, used as keys: attaching a value to one of them is how this program records which part that value plays.
Which keys a value carries is a compile-time fact, tracked through every operation, even though the values attached to them are not.

items.name: Recovered
items.signature: type Recovered = Vec[Concepts; load 1; noisy]
summary: `Recovered` is a name for a value of `Concepts` whose keys the type does not pin down, holding 1 of the 352 items `Concepts` can hold, and not yet matched back to one of them.
notable: The set of keys is left open, so the compiler knows some of what this carries but cannot prove any particular key is absent. Asking for a key that was never attached returns noise, and nothing here can catch that.

Getting a value back out is only approximate: it returns what was asked for plus a little of everything else that was combined with it. Matching it against the space's own entries with `cleanup` is what makes it exact again, and that has not happened here.
